Description: Intrinsic motivation during online learning, 22 items on a 1-7 scale, answered by 1,635 Indonesian students across two samples. Covariates: cov_gender, cov_age, cov_semester, cov_faculty, cov_level, cov_study.
Reference: Agusta, E. (2023). Dataset of Intrinsic Motivation Students while Online Learning in South Sumatera, Indonesia [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.
Notes: The two workbooks are the same instrument on two samples and are merged under cov_study. The header is split across two rows -- section names in row 0, item numbers 1-22 in row 1 -- so the item columns are found by their numbering rather than sliced at a fixed offset, which differs between the files. One row with demographics and no item response at all is dropped; no row is partially answered.

Description: A Digital Health Literacy Scale for undergraduates, 13 items in four subscale blocks on a 1-5 scale, answered by 1,292 Chinese students. Covariates: cov_gender, cov_education_level, cov_region, cov_use_frequency.
Reference: Cao, H., & Chen, P.-F. (2026). Anonymized survey dataset of Digital Health Literacy Scale for Chinese Undergraduate Students [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: One table rather than four: this is the validation sample for one instrument and the four prefixes (DCE, IU, IE, AA) are its subscales, which the deposit never expands, so naming four constructs would be a guess. The prefix stays in the item code. The observed range is 2-5 of a permitted 1-5.

Description: The UEF-1 executive-function self-report, 31 items on a 1-5 scale, answered by 1,092 Cuban university students. Covariates: cov_age, cov_sex, cov_province.
Reference: Díaz Guerra, D. D., Ramos-Galarza, C., Hernández Lugo, M. de la C., & Broche-Pérez, Y. (2024). Validity and Reliability of the Executive Function Scale (UEF-1) in Cuban University Students [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.
Notes: No item text is possible from this deposit: 0 of its 41 variable labels carry a stem, and the populated value labels are option text alone, which irw#1770 forbids shipping. The deposit's F1-F7 factor scores are not shipped.

Description: A 27-item dichotomous Internet Gaming Disorder pool answered by 8,662 Chinese college students, shipped with the study's own 27x9 Q-matrix in qmatrix1-qmatrix9. Covariates: none.
Reference: Liu, S. (2024). Assessing the Diagnostic Precision of the Internet Gaming Disorder Scale (IGD-27) Using Diagnostic Classification Models: An Exploratory Study [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: The Q-matrix maps each item to one of the nine DSM-5 IGD criteria, three items per criterion, joined to the items by row order because that is the only correspondence the deposit provides (IGD_Q.csv has no item column); the script asserts both shapes and the single-attribute structure. The rights register blocks the IGDS9-SF's wording, which does not reach this table: no wording is deposited and response data ships regardless (irw_validate/rights.py).

Description: The Body Appreciation Scale, 10 items on a 1-7 scale, answered by 961 Chinese adolescents (study 2). Covariates: cov_age, cov_gender, cov_grade, cov_origin, cov_social_media_use.
Reference: Liu, X., Zhang, K., Cao, Y., & Chen, S. (2025). Social Media Use, Body Image, and Self-Esteem Among Chinese Adolescents: Experimental and Survey Data (N = 1,113) [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: The deposit's BASsum equals the block sum for all 961 respondents. Only the first column of each block carries a label, and it names the instrument rather than the item, so no item text is extractable.

Description: A self-esteem scale, 10 items on a 1-4 scale, answered before and after an image-exposure manipulation by 152 Chinese middle-school students (study 1). Covariates: cov_age, cov_gender, cov_grade, cov_origin, cov_social_media_use, cov_group.
Reference: Liu, X., Zhang, K., Cao, Y., & Chen, S. (2025). Social Media Use, Body Image, and Self-Esteem Among Chinese Adolescents: Experimental and Survey Data (N = 1,113) [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: Two waves on `wave`: the deposit's B* and G* blocks share the label "Self-Esteem Scale" and the same four value labels, and its pre- and post-test totals equal the B and G sums respectively for all 152 respondents, which is what identifies which block is which. Two responses coded 7 on a 1-4 scale are dropped as out of range; the deposit's own totals include them, which is one reason no total is shipped. cov_group is the 2x2 image condition (38 respondents per cell).

Description: A self-esteem scale, 10 items on a 1-5 scale, answered by 961 Chinese adolescents (study 2). Covariates: cov_age, cov_gender, cov_grade, cov_origin, cov_social_media_use.
Reference: Liu, X., Zhang, K., Cao, Y., & Chen, S. (2025). Social Media Use, Body Image, and Self-Esteem Among Chinese Adolescents: Experimental and Survey Data (N = 1,113) [Dataset]. figshare.
Notes: The deposit's SEsum equals the block sum for all 961 respondents. Labelled only "SE" at the block level; almost certainly the RSES but the deposit does not say.

Description: The RCADS short form, 15 items on a 0-3 scale, answered by 918 English students aged 13-19. Covariates: cov_school, cov_gender, cov_age, cov_year_group, cov_ethnicity, cov_free_school_meals.
Reference: Putwain, D. (2020). Test Anxiety, Wellbeing, Generalised Anxiety and Panic [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.

Description: Adaptability, 9 items on a 1-5 scale, answered twice by 1,192 English students aged 16-19. Covariates: cov_school, cov_gender, cov_age, cov_ethnicity.
Reference: Putwain, D. (2022). Test Anxiety, Wellbeing, Buoyancy, Adaptability, and Mental Health Risk [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.
Notes: Two waves on `wave` (the deposit's unprefixed columns are time 1, its T2* columns the same items at time 2), with the item name carrying no wave so one item links across both. Description: The Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, 10 items on a 1-7 scale, answered in Spanish by 1,317 Peruvian university students. Covariates: cov_sex, cov_age, cov_programme, cov_university.
Reference: Yana-Calla, V. R. (2025). Psychometric properties of the emotional regulation questionnaire in Peruvian university students [Dataset]. Mendeley Data.

Description: Dot-number discrimination with confidence (Rouault et al. 2018, Expt 1): 498 online adults, 210 trials each; which of two boxes held more dots, then an 11-point confidence rating.
Reference: Rouault, M., Seow, T., Gillan, C. M., & Fleming, S. M. (2018). Psychiatric symptom dimensions are associated with dissociable shifts in metacognition but not task performance. Biological Psychiatry, 84(6), 443-451.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Rouault_2018_Expt1.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 certainly wrong to 11 certainly correct); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = dot difference between boxes. Stimulus codes 0/1 kept as s0/s1 (the readme does not say which side is which).

Description: Dot-number discrimination with confidence (Rouault et al. 2018, Expt 2): 497 online adults, 210 trials each, difficulty set by a staircase; 6-point confidence.
Reference: Rouault, M., Seow, T., Gillan, C. M., & Fleming, S. M. (2018). Psychiatric symptom dimensions are associated with dissociable shifts in metacognition but not task performance. Biological Psychiatry, 84(6), 443-451.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Rouault_2018_Expt2.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 guessing to 6 certainly correct); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = dot difference in log units, staircased per person, so items are sparse. Stimulus codes 0/1 kept as s0/s1.

Description: Majority judgements with confidence (Haddara & Rahnev 2022, Expt 1): 443 MTurk adults judged whether X or O (task 1, 330 trials) or red or blue (task 2, 150 trials) dominated a 7x7 grid.
Reference: Haddara, N., & Rahnev, D. (2022). The impact of feedback on perceptual decision-making and metacognition: Reduction in bias but no change in sensitivity. Psychological Science, 33(2), 259-275.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Haddara_2022_Expt1.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here task x majority class), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1-4); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. No stimulus level is recorded, so the table has 4 items (task x majority class). treat = randomly assigned to trial-by-trial feedback; task 2 had no feedback for either group.

Description: Dot-number discrimination with confidence (Jaquiery & Yeung, unpublished, collected 2018): 328 Prolific adults; decision and confidence given together on one slider.
Reference: Jaquiery, M., & Yeung, N. (unpublished). Exploring Social Metacognition: Dot Task (data collected 2018). https://osf.io/qtngm/
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Jaquiery_unpub.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1-50, signed toward the chosen side); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = dots moved from one box to the other. rt is the single decision-plus-confidence response time. Initial decisions from a judge-advisor paradigm, before advice.

Description: Contrast discrimination with confidence (Prieto, Reyes & Silva, unpublished): 204 Chilean mothers aged 18-35, 200 trials each, two-interval task after Fleming et al. (2010), contrast staircased.
Reference: Prieto, F., Reyes, G., & Silva, J. (unpublished). Metacognitive capacity and attachment in mothers. Contributed to the Confidence Database.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Prieto_unpub.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (continuous 1 sure error to 6 sure correct); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = contrast (0.01 grid), staircased per person, so items are sparse. RTs of 2 s or more were not recorded by the task (missing rt). Two rows recorded at a negative contrast were dropped.

Description: Gabor orientation discrimination with confidence (Bang, Shekhar & Rahnev 2019, Expt 2): 201 MTurk adults, 100 coarse (45 deg, in noise) and 100 fine (~1 deg) trials each; 4-point confidence.
Reference: Bang, J. W., Shekhar, M., & Rahnev, D. (2019). Sensory noise increases metacognitive efficiency. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 148(3), 437-452.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Bang_2019_Exp2.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here task x stimulus x catch trial), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 chance to 4 perfectly sure); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = task x stimulus x catch trial (8 items). Contrast (coarse) or tilt (fine) was fixed per batch of subjects and is kept per trial as trial_stim_level. cov_excluded_in_paper flags subjects 179-201, whom the paper excluded for poor performance. Stimulus codes 0/1 kept as s0/s1.

Description: Masked face-sex identification with awareness ratings (Wierzchon et al. 2014): 155 adults, 384 trials each, 12 exposure durations (16-192 ms); one of four awareness scales per person.
Reference: Wierzchon, M., Paulewicz, B., Asanowicz, D., Timmermans, B., & Cleeremans, A. (2014). Different subjective awareness measures demonstrate the influence of visual identification on perceptual awareness ratings. Consciousness and Cognition, 27, 109-120.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Wierzchon_2014.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1-4; meaning depends on cov_scale); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level d1-d12 = exposure 192 down to 16 ms. cov_scale is the between-subject awareness scale as the source codes it (C, O, P, PAS; the readme names confidence rating, PAS, post-decision wagering and feeling of warmth); cov_order = rating before (SD) or after (DS) the decision.

Description: Contrast comparison of two Gabors under monetary incentives, with incentivised confidence (Lebreton et al. 2018, four experiments): 104 adults.
Reference: Lebreton, M., Langdon, S., Slieker, M. J., Nooitgedacht, J. S., Goudriaan, A. E., Denys, D., van Holst, R. J., & Luigjes, J. (2018). Two sides of the same coin: Monetary incentives concurrently improve and bias confidence judgments. Science Advances, 4(5), eaaq0668.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Lebreton_2018.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (50-100% in 5% steps); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = experiment x incentive (G gain, L loss, N neutral, with stake) x side of the higher-contrast Gabor; the four experiments had different people, so items do not overlap across them. Source ids 22XX were folded into 21XX (same people, per the readme). Both contrasts are kept per trial.

Description: Dot-number discrimination with incentivised confidence (Massoni & Roux 2017): 120 adults in Paris, 50 trials each; exposure 850, 700 or 550 ms.
Reference: Massoni, S., & Roux, N. (2017). Optimal group decision: A matter of confidence calibration. Journal of Mathematical Psychology, 79, 121-130.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Massoni_2017.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (0-100% in 5% steps); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level d1-d3 = exposure 850, 700, 550 ms. Two samples: cov_study 1 (trial feedback, d1 or d3 between subjects) and 2 (no feedback, d2); not randomised. Stimulus codes kept as s1/s2.

Description: Dot discrimination with confidence, expectation cues and reward cues (Zheng, Xue, Shekhar & Rahnev 2023): 319 adults, 700 trials each across five conditions.
Reference: Zheng, Y., Xue, K., Shekhar, M., & Rahnev, D. (2023). A common computational principle for decision-making with confidence, expectation and reward. Journal of Vision, 23(9), 4954 (VSS abstract).
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Zheng_2023.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here condition x cue x side), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 = 50-75%, 2 = 75-100%; confidence condition only); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = condition x cue x correct side. Conditions: conf (confidence reported), expect_pre/post and reward_pre/post (cue before or after the stimulus; no confidence). Cue neutral (1:1) or favouring a side (3:1).

Description: Numerosity estimation with confidence (Xiang, Graeber, Enke & Gershman 2021): 300 online adults typed an estimate of 15-65 dots shown for 100 or 2000 ms, 240 trials each, then rated confidence 0-10.
Reference: Xiang, Y., Graeber, T., Enke, B., & Gershman, S. J. (2021). Confidence and central tendency in perceptual judgment. Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics, 83, 3024-3034.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Xiang_2021.csv. One row per trial. resp = the typed estimate (continuous); item = true number of dots x exposure (itemcov_level = true number); rt in seconds; trial_confidence 0-10. Missing estimates (no answer in 10 s) and one negative estimate were dropped; a few very large estimates are kept as recorded. trial_block_mean = that block's mean numerosity (blocks centred on a randomly drawn mean).

Description: Masked discrimination (up- vs down-facing cube) with continuous confidence (Mazor, Moran & Fleming 2021, Expt 5): Prolific adults, 96 trials each.
Reference: Mazor, M., Moran, R., & Fleming, S. M. (2021). Metacognitive asymmetries in visual perception. Neuroscience of Consciousness, 2021(1), niab005.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Mazor_2021_Expt5.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (continuous 0-1); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = stimulus-mask SOA in ms, staircased per person, so items are sparse. Stimulus codes 1/2 kept as s1/s2 (the readme names the two classes but not which code is which).

Description: Gabor orientation discrimination with confidence, response hand cued per trial (Bocheva & Rahnev 2025, Expt 2): 51 lab adults, 1,000 trials each.
Reference: Bocheva, M., & Rahnev, D. (2025). Switching the motor response weakens confidence serial dependence. PsyArXiv.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Bocheva_unpub_Expt2.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here hand x contrast x tilt), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1-4); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = cued hand x contrast (low, high) x tilt (left, right); 8 items. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Average-colour discrimination (red vs blue) with confidence and optional resampling (Desender, Boldt & Yeung 2018, Expt 2): 50 adults, about 640 main trials each.
Reference: Desender, K., Boldt, A., & Yeung, N. (2018). Subjective confidence predicts information seeking in decision making. Psychological Science, 29(5), 761-778.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Desender_2018_Exp2.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here variance x mean distance x class), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (0-50, distance from guess; the readme describes it as 50-100); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = element variance (low, high) x distance of the mean colour from 0.5 (d0-d0.03) x class (s0/s1). Practice rows and 189 rows with no stimulus dropped. rt covers decision and confidence together. trial_condition: 0 forced to respond, 1 chose to respond, 3 chose to see the stimulus again. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Dot-number discrimination with confidence, staircased (Desender, Vermeylen & Verguts 2022, Expt 2B): 99 online adults, 500 trials each.
Reference: Desender, K., Vermeylen, L., & Verguts, T. (2022). Dynamic influences on static measures of metacognition. Nature Communications, 13, 4208.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Desender_2022_Exp2B.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 certainly wrong to 6 certainly correct); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = dot difference, staircased per person, so items are sparse. Stimulus codes kept as s0/s1. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Motion-direction and colour-majority judgements on random-dot kinematograms in single- and dual-task blocks, with confidence (Konishi et al. 2019): 93 lab adults, 540 trials each.
Reference: Konishi, M., Compain, C., Berberian, B., Sackur, J., & de Gardelle, V. (2019). Metacognition is spared in a dual-task visual paradigm. PsyArXiv.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Konishi_2019.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here experiment x block type x task x answer), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (50 guess to 100 certain); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = experiment x single/dual block x task (motion, colour) x correct answer. A dual-task trial gives two rows (one per decision) sharing trial_number. Motion coherence and colour difficulty were staircased and are kept per trial as trial_stim_level. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Dot-number discrimination with incentivised confidence (Massoni, unpublished, collected 2018): 50 lab adults, 200 trials each, two difficulty levels.
Reference: Massoni, S. (unpublished). Dot discrimination with confidence (data collected 2018). Contributed to the Confidence Database.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Massoni_unpub.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (0-100% in 10% steps); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level d1 = twice, d2 = half the person's staircased dot difference. cov_study 1 (no trial feedback, subjects 1-23) and 2 (feedback); separate samples, not randomised. Stimulus codes kept as s1/s2. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Peripheral Gabor and central letter detection under full or diverted attention, with confidence, in patients with functional or organic movement disorder and controls (Matthews et al. 2018): 60 adults.
Reference: Matthews, J., Nagao, K. J., Ding, C., Newby, R., Kempster, P., & Hohwy, J. (2018). Impaired perceptual sensitivity with intact attention and metacognition in functional motor disorder. PsyArXiv.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Matthews_unpub.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here task x attention x expectation x presence), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 complete guess to 4 absolutely certain); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = task (periph Gabor, central letter) x attention (full, diverted) x cued target probability (peripheral only) x target present/absent. A dual-task trial gives two rows. Training blocks dropped. Peripheral contrast and central SOA are kept per trial as trial_stim_level; the central task recorded no RT. cov_group = control, functional or organic movement disorder (20 each). Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Dot-number discrimination at two fixed difficulties, with confidence or feedback on alternate trials (Rouault, Dayan & Fleming 2019): 73 online adults, 360 trials each.
Reference: Rouault, M., Dayan, P., & Fleming, S. M. (2019). Forming global beliefs about self-performance from local confidence. Nature Communications, 10, 1141.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Rouault_2019.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (continuous 50-100%); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = dot difference 24 (hard) or 60 (easy). trial_feedback = 1 marks the trials that gave feedback instead of a confidence rating. All 73 recruited subjects are included; the paper analysed 46 after exclusions. Stimulus codes kept as s0/s1. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Two-interval odd-Gabor contrast detection with confidence, staircased, in methadone-maintenance patients and controls (Sadeghi et al. 2017): 50 men, 180 trials each.
Reference: Sadeghi, S., Ekhtiari, H., Bahrami, B., & Ahmadabadi, M. N. (2017). Metacognitive deficiency in a perceptual but not a memory task in methadone maintenance patients. Scientific Reports, 7, 7052.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Sadeghi_2017_perception.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1 very unsure to 6 very sure); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = contrast difference of the odd Gabor, staircased, so items are sparse. cov_group = patient (opiate dependence, methadone maintenance) or control. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Go/no-go dot comparison with confidence (Siedlecka, Koculak & Paulewicz 2021): 54 students, 780 trials each; press only when the designated side has more dots.
Reference: Siedlecka, M., Koculak, M., & Paulewicz, B. (2021). Confidence in action: Differences between perceived accuracy of decision and motor response. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 28, 1698-1706.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Siedlecka_2021.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level (here designated side x answer x difficulty), with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (1-4); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Item = designated side x side with more dots x difficulty (d1 55:45, d2 52:48, d3 51:49). resp = accuracy, so a correct withhold is correct; trial_response = pressed (1) or withheld (0), and rt is missing on withholds. trial_error_report = 1 where the person reported an error instead of rating confidence. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).

Description: Masked Gabor orientation discrimination with awareness ratings on one of three scales (Wierzchon et al. 2019): 71 adults, four exposure durations.
Reference: Wierzchon, M., Anzulewicz, A., Hobot, J., Paulewicz, B., & Sackur, J. (2019). In search of the optimal measure of awareness: Discrete or continuous? Consciousness and Cognition, 75, 102798.
Notes: Data taken from the Confidence Database (Rahnev et al., 2020, Nature Human Behaviour, doi:10.1038/s41562-019-0813-1; osf.io/s46pr, CC0), file data_Wierzchon_2019.csv. One row per trial. resp = decision accuracy (1 correct, 0 error); item = stimulus class x stimulus level, with the numeric level in itemcov_level where it varies; rt = decision RT in seconds; trial_confidence = confidence on the source's own scale (0-1; meaning depends on cov_scale); trial_response = the alternative chosen, as the source codes it. Level = exposure 32, 48, 64 or 128 ms. cov_scale is between subjects: pas (four categories), cs (continuous), cpas (continuous with PAS labels). Stimulus codes kept as s1/s2. Included under the psychophysics floor of 50 people (#3686).
